title: Guardrail rule form
description: One manager rule, filled in as a form. convert.py turns it into a Dogwood policy. Action and field names come from the action schema (4_rules/schema.cedarschema, a copy of Kylie's testbed schema).

id.description: Becomes the Dogwood @id. Shown to the agent when the rule blocks it.

sentence.description: The manager's original plain-English rule. Copied into a comment.

action.description: The tool call this rule guards, e.g. IssueRefund.

only_when.description: Optional. The rule only applies when this holds (e.g. amount > 100).

field.description: limit/allowlist: the input field being checked.

requires.description: requires_prior: an earlier call that must have happened first. Becomes a permit (Kylie style); only one per action.

within.description: How long ago counts as recent, e.g. 1h. There is no default: 'recently' must be a number.

same.description: Input fields that must match between the earlier call and this one (e.g. order_id, amount).

output.description: Result fields the earlier call must have returned (e.g. approved: true).

output_same.description: Map prior result fields to current inputs, e.g. approved_amount to amount (exact match).

at_most.description: Map current inputs to checked facts they must not exceed, e.g. amount to approved_amount. The fact comes from the context engine (context.facts); with no facts the rule blocks.

approver_role.description: Optional. The role the approver must have in the store's staff directory, e.g. manager (checked through context.facts.approver_role).
